As signed incidence forms for the fan graph over a grounded hub, three-element circuits are exactly consecutive triangles {u_i,u_{i+1},v_i}. For n≥3 their intersection graph is a path, whose automorphisms are identity/reversal R; after fixing triangles, central u_i are distinguished by overlap and only endpoint swaps remain. Circuit relation coefficients (1/a,1/a,1/b) prohibit endpoint radial/edge exchanges when a≠b, leaving precisely ±I,±R. When a=b, explicit independent endpoint involutions L,H realize both swaps; L,H commute and R conjugates L to H, generating eight unsigned maps times global sign, group C2×((C2×C2)⋊C2) of order16. n=2 has one triangle with 6 permutations and global sign -> order12 exactly when a=b; otherwise four. n=1 has just ±I. The exact signed-form enumeration code was examined for use of the whole form family and checks 13 rational finite cases, but all-n proof rests on hyperplane/circuit rigidity.
